content.tex: CONSECUTIVE NUMBERS (36 marks)
This task is about what happens when consecutive numbers are changed from positive to negative and added.
Consecutive numbers are sequences of integers which increase by 1 from term to term.
In this investigation use this method throughout.

\(\bullet\) Add the positive consecutive numbers. \(\bullet\) Find all the possible additions and totals when you make one of the numbers negative. \(\bullet\) Find all the possible additions and totals when you make two of the numbers negative. \(\bullet\) Continue in this way until all the numbers are negative.

parts.text: (c) Anna uses this method to work out the number of integers that cannot be made. • Use Question 4(b) to find the highest total. • Find the number of integers from the highest total to the lowest total. • Use Question 4(a) to find the number of additions. • Subtract the number of additions from the number of integers. Example There are three consecutive numbers. The first number is 4. The highest total is 3 a + 3 = 3 × 4 + 3 = 15. The number of integers from 15 to − 15 is 31. The number of additions is 2 3 . The number of integers that cannot be made is 31 − 2 3 = 23.

content.tex: Anna uses this method to work out the number of integers that cannot be made.

\(\bullet\) Use Question 4(b) to find the highest total. \(\bullet\) Find the number of integers from the highest total to the lowest total. \(\bullet\) Use Question 4(a) to find the number of additions. \(\bullet\) Subtract the number of additions from the number of integers.
\(\frac{Example}{There}\) are three consecutive numbers. The first number is 4.

The highest total is 3a \(+ 3 = 3 \times 4 + 3 = 15.\) The number of integers from 15 to \(-15\) is 31. The number of additions is \(2^{3}\) . The number of integers that cannot be made is \(31 - 2^{3} = 23.\)
